event_changes: Clarified the CMLH109/CMLH110 taxonomy notes to distinguish source-reported isolate genome ANI from species-descriptor reference correspondence (#2848). The source sequenced the six BL6 genomes, but no exact study assembly was independently placed in GTDB in this bounded curation. This note-only intermediate preserves existing statuses, all six stocks, both other grounded blocks and all biological/history content. Separate native mapping and strict composite proof remain pending; prior phenotype/abundance, culture-context and evidence-placement findings remain unresolved.

existing_descriptor.notes: The source identifies CMLH109 as Lactobacillus crispatus; no species-level GTDB classification is asserted here.

notes.before: The source identifies CMLH109 as Lactobacillus crispatus; no species-level GTDB classification is asserted here.
notes.after: The primary study identifies CMLH109 as Lactobacillus crispatus and reports 97.91% ANI to the species type-strain genome in Table 1. Its Methods report whole-genome sequencing of the six BL6 isolates; these are source-reported isolate results, not an independent GTDB placement performed in this curation. Separately, the pinned kg-microbe NCBI2GTDB.tsv.gz reference correspondence (SHA-256 761d5537a7edb4b0133e88e7bbc85570cf3cb6f2555b9f9ce6cca3e1056a0ddd) resolves the exact NCBITaxon:47770 descriptor row to GTDB Lactobacillus crispatus, with 1,123 reference genomes and stored majority fraction 1.0. The crosswalk release is not established. That descriptor population does not identify a CMLH109 study assembly or establish its membership in the reference genomes. The study's on-request data statement does not prove that public accessions are absent; no exhaustive archive search or author contact was performed. Preserve the source stock identity and distinguish database correspondence from experimental abundance or identity probability.

existing_descriptor.notes: The source identifies CMLH110 as Lactobacillus gallinarum; no species-level GTDB classification is asserted here.

notes.before: The source identifies CMLH110 as Lactobacillus gallinarum; no species-level GTDB classification is asserted here.
notes.after: The primary study identifies CMLH110 as Lactobacillus gallinarum and reports 98.05% ANI to the species type-strain genome in Table 1. Its Methods report whole-genome sequencing of the six BL6 isolates; this source evidence is separate from the reference-table calculation. The pinned kg-microbe NCBI2GTDB.tsv.gz reference correspondence (SHA-256 761d5537a7edb4b0133e88e7bbc85570cf3cb6f2555b9f9ce6cca3e1056a0ddd) resolves the exact NCBITaxon:52242 descriptor row to GTDB Lactobacillus gallinarum, with 38 reference genomes and stored rounded majority fraction 0.92. The crosswalk release and exact numerator are not established here. No CMLH110 study assembly was independently placed in GTDB or shown to belong to that reference population in this bounded curation. The source's on-request data statement is not proof of absent public accessions. Preserve the source stock identity; reference counts and fractions are not measured inoculum abundance or probabilities of study-stock identity.

limits: Preparation for exactly two taxonomy notes only. The original overview, DOMINANT annotations, culture-stage omissions and evidence-placement limitations remain as documented in the prior full review; this diagnostic does not clear them or the scientific knowledge-gap discussion. Preserve one community-level node/no arrows, day7/day14 distinctions, relative enrichment versus strain persistence, nominal E.coli-calibrated dose versus viable count, and predicted versus demonstrated effectors. Old batch11 ledger and all other three records' current biology remain intact. An actual note-only application, real maintained intermediate, unchanged mapping engine, eight native gates, immutable partial diagnostic and strict original-to-intermediate-to-final proof are required before admission.
